# ExternalJWTSigner

ExternalJWTSigner is an issuer of JSON Web Tokens, such as an OpenID Connect provider, whose tokens Ziti accepts for authentication. Auth policies refer to it by its name or ID.

| | |
|---|---|
| API version | `ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Namespaced |
| In Ziti | external JWT signer, `/edge/management/v1/external-jwt-signers` |
| Updated with | `PUT`: a setting that is left out of the spec is reset to the default of Ziti |

## Example

From [`examples/externaljwtsigner/externaljwtsigner.yaml`](../../examples/externaljwtsigner/externaljwtsigner.yaml):

```yaml
# An OpenID Connect provider whose tokens Ziti accepts. Ziti gets the keys
# that verify the tokens from jwksEndpoint; a signer without one takes the
# certificate in certPem and its key ID in kid instead.
#
# A token is for the identity whose externalId is the email claim of the
# token, see ../identity/none.yaml. externalAuthUrl, clientId, scopes and
# targetToken tell clients how to obtain a token. The auth policy in
# ../authpolicy/jwt.yaml refers to the signer by its name.
apiVersion: ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: ExternalJWTSigner
metadata:
  name: corporate-sso
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    kind: ProviderConfig
    name: default
  forProvider:
    name: corporate-sso
    issuer: https://sso.example.com/realms/corporate
    audience: ziti
    enabled: true
    jwksEndpoint: https://sso.example.com/realms/corporate/protocol/openid-connect/certs
    claimsProperty: email
    useExternalId: true
    externalAuthUrl: https://sso.example.com/realms/corporate
    clientId: ziti-clients
    scopes:
      - email
      - profile
    targetToken: ID
    tags:
      team: platform
```

## Settings: `spec.forProvider`

| Field | Type | Default | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|------|---------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | string, required |  | `name` | Name of the external JWT signer. |
| `audience` | string, required |  | `audience` | Audience is the aud claim a token must have to be accepted. |
| `issuer` | string, required |  | `issuer` | Issuer is the iss claim of the tokens of this signer. No two signers may have the same issuer. |
| `certPem` | string |  | `certPem` | CertPem is the PEM encoded certificate that verifies the tokens of the signer, for a signer without a JSON Web Key Set. |
| `claimsProperty` | string |  | `claimsProperty` | ClaimsProperty is the claim of a token that tells which identity it is for. Ziti takes the subject if it is not set. |
| `clientId` | string |  | `clientId` | ClientID is the OAuth client ID clients obtain a token with. |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | `enabled` | Enabled makes Ziti accept the tokens of this signer. |
| `enrollAttributeClaimsSelector` | string |  | `enrollAttributeClaimsSelector` | EnrollAttributeClaimsSelector is the claim of a token that holds the role attributes of the identity an enrollment creates. |
| `enrollAuthPolicyId` | string |  | `enrollAuthPolicyId`, as an ID | EnrollAuthPolicyID is the name or ID of the auth policy of the identities an enrollment creates. Ziti takes the default auth policy if it is not set. |
| `enrollNameClaimsSelector` | string |  | `enrollNameClaimsSelector` | EnrollNameClaimsSelector is the claim of a token that names the identity an enrollment creates. Ziti takes the subject if it is not set. |
| `enrollToCertEnabled` | boolean |  | `enrollToCertEnabled` | EnrollToCertEnabled lets the holder of a token of this signer enroll, which creates an identity that authenticates with a certificate. |
| `enrollToTokenEnabled` | boolean |  | `enrollToTokenEnabled` | EnrollToTokenEnabled lets the holder of a token of this signer enroll, which creates an identity that authenticates with tokens of this signer. |
| `externalAuthUrl` | string |  | `externalAuthUrl` | ExternalAuthURL is the URL clients obtain a token of this signer from. |
| `jwksEndpoint` | string |  | `jwksEndpoint` | JwksEndpoint is the URL of the JSON Web Key Set of the signer. It must name a host, and its scheme must be http or https, in any case. Must match `^[Hh][Tt][Tt][Pp][Ss]?://([^/?#@]*@)?(\[[0-9A-Fa-f:.]+\]\|[^/?#@:\[\]]+)(:[0-9]*)?([/?#].*)?$`. |
| `kid` | string |  | `kid` | Kid is the key ID of the certificate in certPem: the kid header of the tokens it verifies. |
| `scopes` | list of strings |  | `scopes` | Scopes are the OAuth scopes clients request a token with. |
| `tags` | map of strings |  | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |
| `targetToken` | string | `ACCESS` | `targetToken` | TargetToken is the token clients present to Ziti: the access token or the ID token. One of `ACCESS`, `ID`. |
| `useExternalId` | boolean |  | `useExternalId` | UseExternalID looks the identity up by its externalId instead of its ID. |

The settings every managed resource has, such as `spec.providerConfigRef`,
`spec.managementPolicies` and `spec.writeConnectionSecretToRef`, are described
in [Concepts](../concepts.md).

## How it behaves

- A signer verifies tokens either with the keys of `jwksEndpoint` or with the certificate in `certPem`, whose key ID is `kid`. Exactly one of the two is set.
- A signer is replaced with `PUT`: a `PATCH` cannot remove a setting, which a signer that changes from `jwksEndpoint` to `certPem` needs. A setting that is left out of the spec is removed in Ziti or reset to its default.
- Ziti ignores the tags of a signer that is being created; the provider sets them with an update right after.
- Ziti does not delete a signer that an auth policy refers to. The resource reports the conflict and is deleted once the policy is gone.
- A signer with `useExternalId: false` finds identities by their Ziti ID. While such a signer is enabled and allowed by an auth policy, the identities under that policy count as able to sign in, and their expired enrollment tokens are not replaced; see [`Identity`](identity.md).

## When something goes wrong

- `CAN_NOT_DELETE_REFERENCED_ENTITY` in `Synced` while deleting: an [`AuthPolicy`](authpolicy.md) still names the signer.
- Ziti answers `400` about the issuer: another signer has the same `issuer`.
- The API server rejects the manifest with `exactly one of jwksEndpoint and certPem is required`, or because `jwksEndpoint` is not an `http` or `https` URL with a host.

Create, update, drift, deletion in Ziti and deletion of the resource are covered by the end-to-end test, see [Testing](../testing.md).
